summary: Granite County lookout tower built about 1938-39 (one source says 1933); its cab moved to Missoula in 1978 and no source describes the original site today.

facts.design: 50-foot cable-braced round timber tower (plan L-11) with an L-4 cab
facts.status_note: The cab was moved to the Missoula Smokejumper Visitor Center; no source describes what became of the tower below it

corrections.why: Firelookout.com dates the cab's move to the visitor center to 1978.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com says constructed in 1933. Forest Lookouts quotes 1938 road work, a plan completed by late 1938 or early 1939, and an October 1939 item saying the tower was erected. The story uses 1938-39 and marks 1933 as disputed.
Firelookout.com calls it a 50-foot L-4 tower; Forest Lookouts names plan L-11 with an L-4 cab. Both agree on the L-4 cab.
The October 1977 report describes disassembly and a planned move; firelookout.com dates the move to 1978. Both fit.

notes_for_editor: The brief's events line reads 'None relocated', but the record has a relocated event with no year; corrections propose 1978. The sibling record us-mt-blackpine-mountain-at-missoula-smokejumper-visitor-center says kind ground and status standing, while the Forest Service page only says the visitor center is closed for renovations, so display of the cab is unconfirmed. The first source_pages entry is an internal relative link, so the Forest Service page was used instead. One web search for the original site today found nothing usable. Newspaper dates and quotes come from the Forest Lookouts page; the newspapers themselves were not read.
